name: Yampa River
agency: Dinosaur National Monument, River Permit Office

camps.name: Deerlodge Park
camps.desc: 7 sites. Pre-launch campground at the put-in: seven walk-in sites, first come first served, seasonal water and vault toilets.

camps.name: Ponderosa
camps.desc: 1 site. Ponderosa Beach; ponderosa pines line this part of the canyon.

camps.name: Tepee Hole
camps.desc: 1 site. At Tepee Beach, just above Tepee Rapid.

camps.name: Big Joe
camps.desc: 1 site. Big Joe Beach, in Starvation Valley by the rapid.

camps.name: Harding Hole
camps.desc: 4 sites. Several groups camp here, with marked site boundaries. Quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Trail to Wagon Wheel Point and Signature Cave.

camps.name: Mather's Hole
camps.desc: 1 site. Beneath a large overhanging cliff, between Big Joe and Warm Springs.

camps.name: Laddie Park
camps.desc: 2 sites. A common camp after Mantle Cave and before Tiger Wall.

camps.name: Warm Springs
camps.desc: 1 site. Camp at the rapid. Filter water here.

camps.name: Box Elder
camps.desc: 3 sites. Box Elder Beach, just above the confluence with the Green.

camps.name: Sea Cliff
camps.desc: 1 site. Below Echo Park, in the upper Whirlpool Canyon reach. Mile is an estimate.

camps.name: Jones Hole
camps.desc: 4 sites. Water can be filtered at Jones Creek. Marked site boundaries.

camps.name: Island Park
camps.desc: 1 site. In the flatwater of Island Park, with views of Split Mountain.

rapids.name: Anderson Hole
rapids.desc: An easy drop just after the box canyon opens, with a wide horizon line and some play waves.

rapids.name: Tepee Rapid
rapids.desc: A wave train with large holes at high water. Tepee Beach is at the rapid.

rapids.name: Little Joe Rapid
rapids.desc: Listed in a river log without a rating.

rapids.name: Five Springs Rapid
rapids.desc: Listed in a river log without a rating; Five Springs Draw enters here.

rapids.name: Big Joe
rapids.desc: The river constricts and rocky debris makes a rapid of waves and holes. Barely runnable at very low flows; scout from river right.

rapids.name: Warm Springs Rapid
rapids.desc: The biggest rapid on the Yampa, formed by a 1965 flash flood down Warm Springs Draw. Scout from river right. Maytag, the last hole, can flip rafts or hold swimmers, and a flip often means a rough night and lost gear. Much tamer at low flows.

rapids.name: Moonshine Rapid
rapids.desc: In Split Mountain Gorge. Not rated individually; the gorge is Class II to III. Life jackets required.

rapids.name: S.O.B. Rapid
rapids.desc: In Split Mountain Gorge. Not rated individually.

rapids.name: Schoolboy Rapid
rapids.desc: In Split Mountain Gorge. Not rated individually.

rapids.name: Inglesby Rapid
rapids.desc: The last rapid in Split Mountain Gorge, just above the take-out. Not rated individually.

hikes.name: Stubs Cabin
hikes.desc: A historic cabin a short walk from the river near Anderson Hole.

hikes.name: Wagon Wheel Point and Signature Cave
hikes.desc: A longer hike from Harding Hole up to the rim viewpoint. Signature Cave holds Fremont artifacts and historic names, including marks left by Pat Lynch between the 1880s and 1917.

hikes.name: Pat's Cave
hikes.desc: A hike across from Mantle Ranch.

hikes.name: Mantle Cave
hikes.desc: Fremont ruins and artifacts. Visitors are welcome; take pictures only.

hikes.name: Tiger Wall
hikes.desc: A tiger-striped, varnished wall rising straight from the water. Boaters traditionally kiss it for luck before Warm Springs Rapid.

hikes.name: Echo Park petroglyphs and Whispering Cave
hikes.desc: Rock art, Pat Lynch inscriptions and Whispering Cave in the Echo Park area, below Steamboat Rock. Pool Creek enters here.

hikes.name: Jones Hole
hikes.desc: A longer hike up Jones Creek with rock art and a waterfall.

indigenous: The river takes its name from the yampa, a wild root dug and eaten by the Ute people. Ute peoples have used this river corridor for centuries and remain connected to the land.

About a thousand years ago the Fremont culture built granaries and shelters and left rock art in the canyons. Mantle Cave holds Fremont ruins and artifacts. Photograph only, and never touch the walls or remove a single piece.
history: John Wesley Powell’s 1869 expedition camped at the confluence below Steamboat Rock and named Echo Park for the way the cliffs sent back their voices. The expedition floated the Green down through Whirlpool Canyon and Split Mountain.
Pat Lynch left his name and inscriptions on the rock near Echo Park, close to Whispering Cave.

In the 1950s the Bureau of Reclamation proposed dams at Echo Park and Split Mountain that would have flooded these canyons. A national campaign led by the Sierra Club’s David Brower stopped them in 1956, and the fight helped launch the modern environmental movement.
A flash flood down Warm Springs Draw in 1965 dumped boulders into the Yampa and created what is now the river’s biggest rapid.
geology: Sandstone walls of the Yampa Canyon

The river flows northwest across tilted beds, cutting steadily down through older and older rock. The upper walls are Weber Sandstone, about 900 feet thick, pale and loosely cemented. Below it lies the Morgan Formation, about 1,200 feet of sandstone and limestone, over the Round Valley limestone, laid down in the Pennsylvanian and early Permian roughly 300 million years ago. Where the soft shale in the Morgan gives way, the cliffs above collapse as landslides.
Where the Yampa meets the Green
The Yampa joins the Green near Echo Park in a triangular, down-dropped block (a graben) between the Mitten Park and Red Rock faults. Farther down, the Green cuts through the Split Mountain anticline.
flows: The National Park Service calls the Yampa the only remaining free-flowing tributary in the Colorado River system, so its flow follows the snowmelt. It typically peaks in late May or early June and drops fast, leaving a short rafting season that runs from the start of runoff into early summer.

Riverbrain lists a recommended flow of about 1,000 cfs minimum to 20,000 cfs maximum for Warm Springs Rapid. Its line changes with flow, and the usual advice is to scout from river right and stay right as you enter.

rules.d: In the high-use season you camp only in the sites assigned to your trip; campsites for the whole trip are registered at the put-in. In the low-use season sites are first come, first served.
Pack up, load boats and clear the landing by noon so the next group can use the site.
No camping on multiday trips at Echo Park, Rainbow Park or in Split Mountain Gorge.
One group per campsite, with up to 25 participants. Where sites are grouped, as at Jones Hole and Harding Hole, stay inside your assigned site; posts mark the boundaries.
The Superintendent may close campsites for bighorn lambing, bear activity or wildfire.
Carry the printed, signed permit and the permit holder's ID, plus the NPS boater's guide.
A fire pan with a 2.5-inch lip and at least 12 inches wide, with a fire blanket.
A river toilet system (groover or day-use kit).

One life jacket per person, plus one spare per 10 people. Spare paddles or oars: one per raft, plus one per three small craft. Helmets for small craft, plus one extra per three craft. Life jackets are required from Rainbow Park to the take-out.
Rafts need three chambers. Soap is restricted to use in the main river flow.
Bear-proof your food storage. Pets are not allowed on the river.

landmarks.name: Deerlodge Park boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Put-in on river left, with a ranger station, information, vault toilets and seasonal water. Campsites for the whole trip are registered here.

landmarks.name: Yampa Canyon
landmarks.desc: The river enters a box canyon almost right away.

landmarks.name: Vale of Tears
landmarks.desc: On river right, per the mile log.

landmarks.name: Disappointment Draw
landmarks.desc: A side draw on river left.

landmarks.name: Mantle Ranch and Hell's Canyon
landmarks.desc: Private land on river left; the ranch is still operating.

landmarks.name: Echo Park and Green River confluence
landmarks.desc: The Yampa ends here and the trip continues down the Green around Steamboat Rock. The road-access campground is not for multiday river trips, and the tap was dry in one trip report. Vehicle access is for emergencies only.

landmarks.name: Steamboat Rock
landmarks.desc: The massive prow the Green River wraps around.

landmarks.name: Whirlpool Canyon
landmarks.desc: About ten miles of canyon on the Green below Echo Park.

landmarks.name: Island Park
landmarks.desc: Long flatwater reach with views of Split Mountain, Ruple Ranch and the occasional moose.

landmarks.name: Rainbow Park boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Not a camp for multiday trips. Life jackets are required from here to the take-out.

landmarks.name: Split Mountain Gorge
landmarks.desc: The river cuts through the gorge in a short, rapid-filled run to the take-out. No camping in the gorge.

landmarks.name: Warm spring
landmarks.desc: A natural warm spring flows into the river.

landmarks.name: Split Mountain boat ramp
landmarks.desc: Take-out. A working dinosaur quarry, museum and gift shop are nearby; the group campground can be reserved on Recreation.gov.

notes.camp: *Camps are assigned by site for the whole trip in the high-use season, and you must be out by noon. Camp high: side-canyon sites can flood in a storm, and bighorn lambing or bear activity can close sites.
notes.hike: *Look at rock art, Fremont ruins and historic inscriptions but never touch or take anything. Side-canyon hikes are hot and flash flood prone; carry water.

access.name: Dinosaur
access.note: Monument headquarters and River Permit Office are in Dinosaur, Colorado

access.name: Deerlodge Park
access.note: Put-in. Campsites, ranger station, vault toilets, seasonal water

access.name: Echo Park
access.note: Road access for emergencies only; not a trip put-in or take-out

access.name: Rainbow Park
access.note: Boat ramp; not for multiday trips

permit.status: Required year-round · lottery for high-use season

items.d: Applications for the high-use season are taken on Recreation.gov from December 1 to January 31. Results are emailed by mid-February. Choose Deerlodge Park as the launch and Split Mountain as the take-out, not the Gates of Lodore Green River option.
Each person may submit one high-use lottery application. Multiple applications forfeit any trip won. Applicants must be at least 18.
Winners confirm and pay the permit fee by the deadline in their results email.
Low-use trips and unclaimed high-use dates open for reservation on March 6 at 8 a.m. Mountain Standard Time.
Campsites for your whole trip are assigned and registered at Deerlodge Park before launch.
Standard high-season Yampa trips are 5 days. You may request one extra day for a $35 fee, refunded if denied. Requests are decided 30 days before launch, after campsites are assigned.
December 1 to January 31, for the following season.
Second Monday of May through the second Saturday of July. The rest of the year is low-use. The season depends on snowmelt, since the Yampa is undammed.
Short day trips below Split Mountain are free and need no reservation.
$185 per trip. Entrance and campground fees are separate.
Permit fees are nonrefundable, except an overlength fee when the extra day is denied.
Up to 25 per site. Outfitter guides recommend 16 or fewer.
Private boaters need qualifying experience and equipment. Trips must be self-guided.
The permit holder must be on the trip and permits are not transferable. Cancellations less than two weeks out carry penalties.
Rafts are runnable above about 1,000 cfs. At very low flows several rapids nearly disappear and Warm Springs is the only real challenge.
